fullPassage: There is no scientific basis for the term 'race'. Most humans are genetically very similar and there is so little variation amongst us that it is not possible to draw neat boundaries around people and label them as a distinct racial group. Race is an example of social construction, where social processes create something that essentially does not exist but takes on real force in people's lives. Sociologists prefer to call these processes 'racialization'. Historical evidence that race has always been an issue is hard to find. For example, in ancient Rome there were various leading figures, such as Emperor Septimius Severus (ruled C.E. 193–211), who were black. Little is said of their skin colour in accounts written at the time, because the ancient Romans did not think it made any difference. They thought more in terms of judging people as being civilized or a barbarian.

questions.passage: There is no scientific (A)[basis / bias] for the term 'race'. Most humans are genetically very similar and there is so little (B)[variation / violation] amongst us that it is not possible to draw neat boundaries around people and label them as a (C)[distinct / extinct] racial group. Race is an example of social construction, where social processes create something that essentially does not exist but takes on real force in people's lives. Sociologists prefer to call these processes 'racialization'.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: '인종'이라는 용어에 대한 과학적 근거(basis)는 없다. 인간은 유전적으로 매우 유사하고 변이(variation)가 매우 적어서 사람들을 뚜렷한(distinct) 인종 집단으로 분류하는 것은 불가능하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① basis — variation — distinct ❌ ② bias — variation — distinct ❌ ③ basis — violation — distinct ❌ ④ basis — variation — extinct ✅①basis — variation — distinct: 원문과 일치
❌②bias(편견): basis(근거)와 다른 의미
❌③violation(위반): variation(변이)과 다른 의미
❌④extinct(멸종한): distinct(뚜렷한)와 반대 맥락
det.tip: basis(근거) vs bias(편견), variation(변이) vs violation(위반), distinct(뚜렷한) vs extinct(멸종한)

questions.passage: Race is an example of social (A)[construction / destruction], where social processes create something that essentially does not exist but takes on real (B)[force / source] in people's lives. Sociologists prefer to call these processes '(C)[racialization / rationalization]'. Historical evidence that race has always been an issue is hard to find. For example, in ancient Rome there were various leading figures, such as Emperor Septimius Severus, who were black.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 인종은 사회적 구성(construction)의 한 예로, 사회적 과정이 본질적으로 존재하지 않는 것을 만들어 내지만 사람들의 삶에서 실질적인 힘(force)을 갖게 된다. 사회학자들은 이러한 과정을 '인종화(racialization)'라고 부르는 것을 선호한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① destruction — force — racialization ✅ ② construction — force — racialization ❌ ③ construction — source — racialization ❌ ④ construction — force — rationalization ✅②construction — force — racialization: 원문과 일치
❌①destruction(파괴): construction(구성)의 반의어
❌③source(원천): force(힘)과 다른 의미
❌④rationalization(합리화): racialization(인종화)과 다른 개념

questions.passage: Historical (A)[evidence / absence] that race has always been an issue is hard to find. For example, in ancient Rome there were various (B)[leading / misleading] figures, such as Emperor Septimius Severus (ruled C.E. 193–211), who were black. Little is said of their skin colour in accounts written at the time, because the ancient Romans did not think it made any (C)[difference / preference].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 인종이 항상 문제가 되어 왔다는 역사적 증거(evidence)를 찾기는 어렵다. 고대 로마에는 다양한 지도적(leading) 인물들이 있었다. 고대 로마인들은 피부색이 어떤 차이(difference)도 만들지 않는다고 생각했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① absence — leading — difference ❌ ② evidence — misleading — difference ✅ ③ evidence — leading — difference ❌ ④ evidence — leading — preference ✅③evidence — leading — difference: 원문과 일치
❌①absence(부재): evidence(증거)와 반대 의미
❌②misleading(오도하는): leading(지도적인)과 다른 의미
❌④preference(선호): difference(차이)와 다른 의미
det.tip: evidence(증거) ↔ absence(부재), leading(지도적인, 주요한), make a difference(차이를 만들다)
